Title: Trapezium Rule for Definite Integrals/Error Term

Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Real Function|real function]] which is [[Definition:Integrable Function|integrable]] on the [[Definition:Closed Real Interval|closed interval]] $\closedint a b$.

Let $P = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n - 1}, x_n}$ form a [[Definition:Normal Subdivision|normal subdivision]] of $\closedint a b$:
:$\forall r \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: x_r - x_{r - 1} = \dfrac {b - a} n$

Let $f$ be [[Definition:Approximation|approximated]] by the [[Trapezium Rule for Definite Integrals|trapezium rule]]:

:$\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x \approx \dfrac h 2 \paren {\map f {x_0} + \map f {x_n} + \sum_{r \mathop = 1}^{n - 1} 2 \map f {x_r} }$

where $h = \dfrac {b - a} n$.

The [[Definition:Error|error]] can be quantified as:
:$\dfrac {\paren {b - a}^3 \map {f' '} \xi} {12 n^2}$
where $\xi \in \closedint a b$.
